problem: A linear transformation $T$ represents a dilation.  Given that $v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}]$ and $T(v)=[\begin{aligned}48 \\ -32\end{aligned}],$ what is the standard matrix of $T?$
worked_solution:
We can write $T(v)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(v) & =[\begin{aligned}48 \\ -32\end{aligned}] \\  & =16\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =16v\end{aligned}
$$

So we have $T(v)=16v,$ and so the linear transformation $T$ is a dilation with scale factor $k=16.$

The matrix that represents a dilation of scale factor $k$ is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}k & 0 \\ 0 & k\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the standard matrix of $T$ is

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}16 & 0 \\ 0 & 16\end{aligned}].
$$
